## Table 7.3 (table; file `R1_hypothesis_scorecard`): Hypothesis scorecard: every pre-registered hypothesis, comparison and check, with its restated verdict

**Caption.** Each row quotes the pre-registered prediction (with its source line), the outcome now (after the final re-runs and the rulings of 2026-10-16) and one of five verdicts. Counts per scored part (48 parts, 35 labels): PASS 24, FAIL AS WORDED 4, NOT MET 17, WITHDRAWN 1, DESCRIPTIVE 2.

*Note.* Verdicts (the rule used here; the record's own word decides): PASS = the record says PASS, MET or TRUE (including a verdict 'accepted as worded'); FAIL AS WORDED = a failure the record itself labels 'as worded' (the literal verdict, kept although the wording is known to be faulty or unbanded; methodology draft, 'As worded'); NOT MET = a test that was run and whose rule was not met, recorded as FAIL, NOT met, FALSE or MISS without that label; WITHDRAWN = no longer made (methodology draft, 'Withdrawn'): V3 is not re-scorable, so its old PASS is listed and not restated; DESCRIPTIVE = no comparative test (C1.a is a pre-registered comparison with no decision rule; X1.b is exploratory).

*Note.* Labels with parts are scored per part (H1.2 by wall type and floor, H1.3 (a)/(b), H1.6b and H1.6c (a)/(b), H1.8 and H1.9 per flying estimator, H5.5 its bands and the S2/S3 directional prediction, H5.6 as pre-registered, as redefined and its jump criterion kept as worded), so the counts are per part, not per label.

*Note.* Experiment 5 (ruling 2026-10-17): every H5 prediction is quoted VERBATIM (no ellipsis; checked unbroken in the cited lines, markdown removed) and its verdict is judged against that wording. H5.1, H5.5, H5.6 (as pre-registered) and H5.7 are quoted from the S0/S1 pre-registration (M:10623, 'written before any H flight'); the H5.6 redefinition and its kept jump criterion from the S2/S3 pre-registration (M:10946, 'before any S2/S3 flight'). H5.2–H5.4b have no METHODOLOGY pre-registration line; their only pre-registration is the design draft (tag_hold_design.md §e), whose text is unchanged since commit c11fcf3 (2026-10-08 15:17), before the first Experiment 5 flight. Two wordings exist for H5.1 and H5.5: the design draft says 'H-H1 (primary): every estimator holds within tag-fix accuracy. Mean hold error ≤ 0.05 m and max ≤ 0.15 m in 3/3 flights per estimator.' (tag_hold_design.md:176-177) and 'P-H5 (drift during loss, prediction): GT drift during the 15 s occlusion ≤ 0.3 m for every estimator.' (tag_hold_design.md:188); the METHODOLOGY wording is the one scored. Both PASS under either wording (flying hold sets 6.1–7.4 / 17–21 mm UKF and 8.1–9.0 / 18–28 mm FGO, numbers.md:644, 646; the draft's P-H5 was scored PASS at M:12243).

*Note.* H5.5 S2/S3 directional prediction (ruling 2026-10-18): 'both flying estimators drift more than flying EKF3 did (3–31 mm)' (M:10971, in the S2/S3 pre-registration), scored as worded on the final builds (final UKF port H_s2v2_r*, final FGO node H_s3v2_r*) against flying EKF3 (the EKF3-flying hold set H_s1_r*, near spawn, the source of the registered 3–31 mm; the EKF3 shadows of the S2/S3 flights are not used), from stored drift values only. Primary: per matched loss (the same loss, 5 / 15 / 30 s hover or ~7 s move, and the same repeat: 12 per estimator), 'more' = strictly greater at full precision, on the effective drift (last fix to first returning fix), the metric of the registered 3–31 mm (M:10827-10828); it holds iff both estimators exceed flying EKF3 in every matched loss. Result: UKF 4 of 12, FGO 9 of 12; the end-of-loss metric gives the same counts; at the displayed mm precision UKF 3 of 12 (one UKF pair, repeat 2, 30 s loss, equal at that precision) and FGO 9 of 12. The ranges overlap (UKF 2–26, FGO 7–27, flying EKF3 3–31 mm). NOT borne out (the predicted outcome did not occur): labelled NOT MET. Caveat (M:12249): each estimator flew its own flights, so the pairing is by run index, not the same trajectory; it also crosses spawn points (the final-build UKF and FGO sets flew from the far spawn). The superseded builds were judged NOT borne out (M:12244-12245).

*Note.* H1.3 is shown as recorded on 2026-09-29 (M:3440-3448): no restated Phase 5 verdict exists after the final re-runs, only the restated decomposition magnitudes (numbers.md:263). The criteria families without hypothesis labels (dataset-quality bands, the 5S safety criteria) are not scored here: numbers.md §8 and Table A.2.

*Note.* 'Changed through the corrections?' names the claims-table row (headline_claims_before_after.md) and the correction number (Table 7.4) where the sources link them. Corrections applied in one batch are applied jointly and not attributed individually (corrections file, attribution rule); a correction number after a change means 'in the batch that contained it', except where marked as a flight pair or a partial attribution.

*Note.* Experiment 3 scope (claims C2 and C3, user ruling 2026-10-24; the H3.1–H3.4 verdicts are unchanged): H3.1–H3.4 were scored with all 8 tags and correct tag IDs. Extension experiments (pre-registered 2026-10-21, signed off with amendments 2026-10-22; not thesis hypotheses, so not rows here): with 4 tags and with 2 tags, loop closure also bounded live drift (H-E2.1 PASS 3/3 in each); with wrong IDs in 1% of the eligible detections, the FGO as built lost its loop-closure advantage (H-E3.1 FAIL 0/9; 6 of 9 runs diverged); a UKF with tag landmark states also bounded its live drift (H-E5.1 PASS 3/3). See limitations list item 3 and docs/thesis/tier1/claims_applied.md.

## Table 7.4 (table; file `R2_corrections_by_discovery`): Corrections grouped by how they were found, with the headline claims and hypotheses each one changed

**Caption.** The 18 corrections of the final results pack (corrections file) and two later ones it does not list (19, 20), grouped by the discovery route the sources record. 'Claims rows' are the rows of the headline-claims table (before vs after the final re-runs); rows are named for the re-run batch that changed them, which applied its corrections jointly.

*Note.* Discovery routes are taken from the corrections file's 'how it was found' column (quoted), or from METHODOLOGY for 19 and 20. The SITL-flight group holds the defects that a flown result exposed: a closed-loop smoke flight (5), a scored closed-loop failure (11), hold flights (14, 16) and the scoring of the first hold flights (20). No correction was discovered by the attribution study itself (it attributed, it did not find); none is recorded as found by a reviewer's or the user's question.

*Note.* Corrections 1–13, 19 and 20 predate the claims table's 'before' state (commit 07f9f56, 2026-10-09 20:03): their effects are inside the 'before' column, so no claims row records them. 14–17 were applied jointly in the first final re-run and 18 alone in the FGO-only re-run; a claims row is listed against the batch that changed it, not attributed to one correction, except the directly traced plain-wall case (row 8, 18 and 14), the ruled O partial attribution (rows 21–22: ≈93% 14, ≈7% 15) and flight 2 of the standard-sensor dataset (17, by elimination).

*Note.* Included beyond the pack's 18: 19, the FGO trajectory-writer typo (D10), which changed stored FGO yaw values (≤ 0.17°) but no numbers.md row at its printed precision; and 20, the re-lock-time redefinition. Excluded (display or transcription fixes, no stored result changed): the single-rounding correction of numbers.md displays and the three transcription corrections (rulings 2026-10-16; M:14229-14247); the 'final safety run' restatement (ruling 2026-10-16 item 5), which re-labels which stored run is final.

## Figure 4.2 (figure; file `R3_trajectory_overlay`): True and estimated paths, top-down: with the camera heading the UKF and FGO paths lie on the true path

**Caption.** Flights chosen by a rule fixed before plotting: (a) of the 9 textured-floor flights of the standard-sensor dataset that all three estimators complete (flights 1–9; flight 10 is unusable for the UKF and FGO), the flight whose mean cruise ATE over EKF3, UKF and FGO is the median (5th of 9); (b) the flight of the textured-wall camera dataset (textured floor) with the same repeat index as (a) if it exists among its flights 1–3, otherwise the median of those three by the mean cruise ATE of the arms drawn solid. Chosen: (a) standard sensors, no heading, standard-sensor dataset, textured floor, flight 3 (cross-estimator mean cruise ATEs, ascending, by flight: 6: 1.85, 2: 2.42, 1: 4.02, 9: 4.46, 3: 4.58, 4: 4.59, 5: 4.62, 7: 4.64, 8: 4.84 m); (b) with the camera heading (offline heading arms), textured-wall camera dataset, textured floor, flight 3 (same repeat index as (a), flight 3). Top-down, cruise window only, truth grey. Each estimated path is drawn after a best-fit rotation about the vertical and a shift (no scale), fitted over the stored cruise window against its own ground-truth file. This gives the same average error as the standard 3D alignment used for the cruise ATE (the RMSE of every plotted path is within 0.005 m of its stored cruise ATE; cross-checks), but cannot roll the path about the corridor axis: the 3D fit is free to do so on a straight path and can turn sideways drift into up-and-down error that is invisible from above. The alignment removes a constant heading offset, so the metres-scale sideways drift of the unaligned estimates (Table 4.1, heading-error decomposition) is not shown; an error along the corridor (for example EKF3's distance-scale error) lies along the path and barely shows top-down. Dashed: no heading source; solid: with the camera heading (offline heading arms, UKF and FGO only; EKF3 has no offline heading arm and is shown as the no-heading baseline). The lateral (East) axis is stretched 3.0× relative to the along-corridor axis, the same in both panels; no log axes. Passive estimators, truth flying (Experiment 1A/1B offline). Cruise ATE (m): (a) EKF3 4.10, UKF 5.17, FGO 4.48 (all no heading); (b) EKF3 4.08 (no heading), UKF 4.96 (no heading) / 0.14 (with heading), FGO 4.54 (no heading) / 0.06 (with heading).

**Inputs.** ~/thesis_data/trials/dsn_tex_r3/{ekf3,ukf,fgo}/*.tum; ~/thesis_data/trials/fwdc_tex_r3/{ekf3,ukf_baseline,fgo_baseline,ukf_heading,fgo_heading}/*.tum; windows and cruise ATEs: eval/results/rerun_dsn_evo.json, dsn_extra_evo.json, phase4_fwdc_evo.json

**Files.** `R3_trajectory_overlay.png`, `R3_trajectory_overlay.pdf`

## Table 7.5 (table; file `R4_information_vs_estimator`): Spread between estimators against the effect of adding information, per condition

**Caption.** For each condition: the primary metric of each estimator, the best–worst spread across the estimators (max − min and max ÷ min), and the change when information is added (a heading, more tags, GNSS, or the tag itself). Spreads and ratios are computed here from the stored full-precision values and rounded once; their inputs are cross-checked against numbers.md. The numbers are reported without a conclusion beyond them.

*Note.* Spread = max − min and max ÷ min of the stated metric over the estimators that have a value in that condition (2 in Experiment 1B with heading and on the blank floor; 3 elsewhere). 'Per flight' ranges are the range over flights of the per-flight spread or ratio. Ratios use the stored full-precision values, not the displayed ones.

*Note.* Experiment 1A's information contrast (a compass, EKF3 only) compares different flights of the same world and is descriptive. Experiment 1B's contrast is paired (the same bags with and without the heading arm); EKF3 has no offline heading arm (by ruling). The plain-wall camera dataset is omitted: on its checkerboard floor the heading failed validation (H1.2), so no heading benefit is claimed there (restatement ruling 4).

*Note.* Blank floor: the +60 s and end-of-cruise values are runaway magnitudes (†, not reproducible across builds), so no ratio is formed from them; +30 s is used. Experiments 4 and 5 compare different statistics across the information contrast (stated in the row), so those ratios are indicative only. Experiment 3 (loop closure) has one thesis estimator and no spread: the thesis EKF3 and UKF, as configured, have no landmark states; a UKF with tag landmark states (extension experiment E5, not in this table) also bounded its live drift (H-E5.1 PASS 3/3). Experiment 1C (closed loop) passes 3/3 for every estimator with the heading (Table 4.3), so it has no spread in its primary metric.

*Note.* Raw (DESCRIPTIVE) column: world-frame position error, nothing fitted (no rotation, translation or scale alignment), RMS and end-of-cruise, 3D (matching evo -a (cruise)'s own pose_relation, the translation part), for the two rows this table shares with Tables 4.1 and 7.1 (Experiment 1A, 1B) - limitations.md item 5; decisions D106, D111; eval/results/raw_corridor_errors.json via docs/thesis/raw_corridor/raw_corridor_numbers.md. '-' marks a row outside the raw-corridor scope (Experiments 2, 4, 5 and the blank floor); it is not a withheld value.

**Inputs.** eval/results/rerun_dsn_evo.json, dsn_extra_evo.json, rerun_ds_evo.json, phase4_fwdc_evo.json, blank_behaviour.json, expT/t_aggregate.json, expO/O_*.json, expH/h_comparative_2026-10-11.json, expH/s1far_r*.json, s2v2_r*.json, s3v2_r*.json, raw_corridor_errors.json (raw column)

**Files.** `R4_information_vs_estimator.md`, `R4_information_vs_estimator.tex`, `R4_information_vs_estimator_p1.png`, `R4_information_vs_estimator_p2.png`

## Gaps: what cannot be built from existing sources (listed, not inferred)

- **H1.3 restated verdict.** No Phase 5 verdict was re-scored after the final re-runs; Table 7.3 shows the 2026-09-29 verdict (M:3440-3448) beside the restated magnitudes (numbers.md:263).
- **X1.b values.** The exploratory robust-vs-hard-gated FGO table (M:8464-8471) predates the final re-runs and has no restated numbers.md row; only its replication (H1.7) is restated.
- **V3.** Not re-scorable (its labels were never recorded; ruling 6, 2026-10-09). It fits none of the five categories exactly; it is counted as WITHDRAWN ('listed, not restated').
- **H5.2–H5.4b pre-registration.** Only the design draft (`docs/tag_hold_design.md` §e) states them; there is no METHODOLOGY pre-registration line.
- **Correction-to-claim attribution.** Corrections applied in one batch (14–17; and 18 alone) are not attributed to individual claims rows except the three ruled exceptions; corrections 1–13, 19 and 20 predate the claims table, so no claims row records their effect.
- **Experiment 4 'with GNSS' accuracy.** No stored outdoor RMSE exists; the error 10 s after GNSS returns (`err_10s_after_return_m`, no numbers.md cell) is the only with-GNSS value, a single time point, not like-for-like with the indoor RMSE.
- **Experiment 5 information contrast.** Hold error (tag visible) and end-of-loss drift (tag hidden) are different statistics; no like-for-like 'without the tag' hold error exists.
- **Blank floor.** Only the non-runaway +10 s and +30 s errors can carry a ratio; the +60 s and end-of-cruise values are † runaway magnitudes.
- **Figure 4.2 unaligned drift.** The paths are drawn after a yaw-only alignment that reproduces the stored cruise ATE to within 0.005 m (ruling 2026-10-21); the unaligned metres-scale sideways drift is the heading-error decomposition of Table 4.1, not redrawn here.
